title: Holiday release mini-runbook and comms clips - Dec 2027 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact runbook for the December quiet-window release: small feature rollouts + performance patch to model routing. Primary goal: keep risk low during holiday traffic dip while exercising canary and rollback paths. Use as the single reference for the 48h window.

Scope and constraints:
- Small traffic percent (0.5% -> 2%) staged canaries.
- No schema changes, only runtime routing and config.
- Targeted regions: us-west1, eu-west1. APAC excluded for this wave.
- SLA-sensitive customers are on hold; we will not target Dedicated clusters used by enterprise customers.

Quick timeline (local times in UTC):
- T-72h: Final sign-off doc posted, security review sanity check done.
- T-48h (2027-12-20 10:00 UTC): Final smoke checklist run; owners assigned.
- T-24h (2027-12-21 10:00 UTC): Canary config baked, low-volume synthetic warmup started.
- T-12h (2027-12-21 22:00 UTC): Night watch handover; traffic ramp plan reviewed.
- T0 (2027-12-22 10:00 UTC): Start 0.5% traffic to canary variant. Monitor 30m intervals.
- T+3h: If stable, increase to 1.5%.
- T+12h: If stable, increase to 2% and begin follow-on checks.
- T+24h: Hold. If no regressions, schedule postmortem + retrospective.

Preflight checklist (must be green before T-24h):
- [ ] Release notes drafted and linked (customer + internal).
- [ ] Canary images built, SHA pinned in release config.
- [ ] Rollout dashboard prepared (per-model, per-route panes).
- [ ] Alerts scoped and muted/annotated where appropriate.
- [ ] Telemetry spikes sampling adjusted for quiet window.
- [ ] Backup config for prefix cache and prewarm script committed.
- [ ] Oncall and release owners assigned in Slack channel #release-holiday-2027.
- [ ] Customer success notified for active enterprise customers (list attached).

Day-of playbook (step-by-step):
0) 09:45 UTC: Final quick sync (15 min) on Zoom; all owners present.
1) 10:00 UTC: Start canary (0.5%). Add annotation to build and record start time.
2) 10:30 UTC: Verify 200/latency/availability per SLO dashboards. Key metrics: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost delta.
3) 11:00 UTC: Quick smoke test: 10 synthetic requests across typical prompt lengths. Log results in the runbook.
4) 12:00 UTC: If green, step to 1.5%. If anomalies, follow rollback matrix.
5) 15:00 UTC: Run routing traffic churn test (simulate burst x1.5) to ensure autoscale paths functional.
6) 22:00 UTC: Night watch handover, annotate any open items.
7) T+24h: Post-checks and start drafting final release notes.

Rollback decision criteria (examples):
- Immediate rollback if: 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, or latency p95 regression > 200ms over baseline and error budget threatened.
- Conditional pause and investigate if: minor error bump (<0.5%) or unexplained increased variance in output quality metrics.
- Owner in charge of rollback: @Tom (release lead). Secondary: @Lina (SRE).

Fast rollback steps:
1) Trigger route-scale-back to 0% for canary variant (Routing Console -> Route: canary -> Set 0%).
2) Repoint traffic to last stable candidate.
3) Re-run critical smoke tests and confirm health.
4) Open an incident ticket and notify #sre and #product-alerts.

Comms snippets (pick one and edit for channel)
- Internal Slack (short):
  "Release: Holiday mini-run. Canary start 2027-12-22 10:00 UTC -> 0.5%. Owners: Aisha/Tom/Lina. Watchlist in dashboard: models X/Y. Rolling per playbook; ping oncall for anomalies. Link: <doc>"

- Customer-facing (email for impacted customers):
  Subject: Planned maintenance & small performance rollout - Dec 22
  Body: Hi — We’ll be rolling a small performance update into a subset of traffic on Dec 22. No action required. Expected impact: none for typical use. If you see issues, reply and we’ll revert. Planned window: 10:00 UTC for 24h.

- Release notes (internal expanded draft):
  "What: routing optimization and config tweak to reduce model switch latency.
   Why: shave 50-100ms p95 on multi-model routing for short-seq workloads.
   Risk: low — no schema or model weight changes.
   Rollout: staged canary 0.5% -> 1.5% -> 2%.
   Rollback plan: route back to stable hash; incident if errors exceed thresholds.
  "

Observability and test matrix (quick):
- Logs: route-annotations enabled; sample rate 100% for canary.
- Metrics: token-serving-latency, model-switch-count, kvcache-hit-rate, 5xx-by-route.
- Traces: distributed traces for canary requests tagged with release_id.
- Quality checks: small eval set (10 prompts) with automated BLEU+embedding-sim checks every hour.

Night watch and handover notes:
- Primary night watcher: Evan (22:00 - 06:00 UTC).
- Handover template: summary, outstanding alerts, time-of-next-check. Use Handover header in this doc and append timestamped notes.

Post-release checklist (within 72h):
- [ ] Capture post-rollout telemetry and compare to baseline.
- [ ] Unmute any alerts manually silenced and annotate why.
- [ ] Draft brief for product + ops: what changed, measured impact, follow-ups.
- [ ] Schedule retrospective + lessons learned meeting (30–60m).

Open items / TODOs:
- Confirm sample rate increase with observability quota team (Evan).
- Add enterprise blacklist to exclude specific customer namespaces from canary (pending CS approval).
- Finish customer notification list (Aisha to finalize).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the canary tiny — holiday traffic low, but anomalies can be noisier.
- If any latency spikes, double-check KV cache warming script; common culprit.
- Remember to annotate every step with UTC timestamp for easy correlation.

References / handy links:
- Jira: REL-1428 (release epic)
- PR: platform#3184 (routing config)
- Slack: #release-holiday-2027, #sre
- Confluence guardrail page (link posted in linked_artifacts)

Contact roster:

- SRE: Lina Márquez (lina@redwood.ai)
- Night watcher: Evan Brooks (evan@redwood.ai)
- Product owner: Tom Nguyen (tom@redwood.ai)
